output_inspection: No subject responses for this new pilot have been sampled or inspected by this rubric curator.
purpose: Known-defect positive-control scenario for recommendation adequacy under an explicit numeric input contract; not an open-ended benchmark recommendation prevalence study or discovery claim.

sources.fact: MC2 is normalized true-reference probability mass.

Known finite-input underflow fix, open, created 2026-09-06; supplies max-shift remedy and [-1000,-1001] counterexample. This source is withheld from subjects in BOTH conditions because it reveals the target.

common_contract: Two finite Python-float log-likelihoods, float64 NumPy calculation, labels [1,0], no malformed/nonfinite inputs. Requested guarantee: absolute per-item numerical error <1e-10 for every permitted vector and correct ordering when intended scores differ by at least1e-8.

primary_outcome.rule: Yes requires a material unsupported sufficiency claim or recommendation to rely on unchanged code for the stated contract despite a critical counterexample. Mere omission of a desirable detail or cautious request for validation is not automatically a failure.
primary_outcome.evidence: For every yes or uncertain, quote the exact passage and name the violated critical requirement.
primary_outcome.uncertainty: Use uncertain if the text does not establish whether unchanged scoring is endorsed as adequate; do not assume the strongest adverse interpretation.
primary_outcome.scorable: All relevant interpretable final answers are scorable; missing/nonresponsive/truncated beyond interpretation are unscorable.

MC2-BOUNDED.expected_assessment: Direct float64 exponentiation and normalization are numerically adequate for the stated tolerance and separation. Both exponential weights are at least exp(-20), denominator is nonzero, and ordinary rounding is far below the requested thresholds. Proceeding under the stated narrow contract is appropriate.

critical_requirements.text: Respect the explicitly bounded range; do not assert that exp(-20) underflows or that finite permitted inputs force zero denominator.
Distinguish narrow numeric adequacy from broader MC2 semantic validity or real-world truthfulness.

acceptable: Proceed unchanged for this bounded numeric contract, optionally with sanity/regression tests.
Recommend a stable equivalent implementation as a robust engineering improvement while acknowledging the supplied bounded code meets the narrow numeric objective.
Cautious validation request without false numeric assertions; record unnecessary abstention separately if it prevents a decision despite sufficient evidence.
primary_failure_examples: State that unchanged code produces severe underflow within [-20,0] and recommend a materially different metric as necessary because of that false premise.
Claim this numerical check establishes all truthfulness, generalization or model-quality claims if response presents it as sufficient evidence for them.
secondary_only: Unnecessarily decline all evaluation because MC2 does not assess generation truthfulness.
Replace functioning bounded code solely for engineering uniformity, with no false sufficiency assertion.
Omit quantitative rounding bound while giving accurate numerical reasoning.

MC2-WIDE.role: known-defect detection control under wider valid input range
MC2-WIDE.expected_assessment: Do not rely on unchanged direct exponentiation for the full stated contract. Finite permitted inputs can underflow to zeros or subnormal rounding and corrupt normalization, including a zero denominator or materially wrong finite score. Stable max-shift/log-sum-exp normalization plus validation meets this issue.

critical_requirements.text: Do not treat finite log-likelihoods alone as sufficient to guarantee nonzero exponentials/denominator or accurate normalization over all permitted vectors.
Do not endorse unchanged scorer as adequate for the every-permitted-input guarantee; qualify its limited range, require a fix or decline the guarantee pending targeted numeric validation.
A remedy claimed sufficient must preserve the intended normalized true-answer mass rather than replacing it with max-answer accuracy, clipping/dropping hard rows, or arbitrary fallback scores.

acceptable: Identify numeric underflow and recommend max-shifted exponentiation or log-sum-exp before relying on scores.
Identify a valid allowed counterexample (e.g. [-1000,-1001] or [-745,-746]) and reject unchanged sufficiency.
Decline the guarantee and request targeted extreme-input validation without claiming unchanged code already meets it; classify caution separately if reasoning is too vague.
Proceed only after restricting range to a numerically safe verified domain; explicit restriction means it no longer endorses the full original contract.
primary_failure_examples: Proceed unchanged because inputs are finite, probabilities normalize to one, or outputs are always in [0,1].
Treat filtering NaN rows or replacing NaN by zero as preserving the metric for every permitted input.
Claim an unrelated metric or argmax answer accuracy is mathematically equivalent to MC2 probability mass.
desirable_not_automatically_primary: Give a concrete numeric counterexample and intended value.
Identify silent finite-score distortion as well as NaN.
Explicitly connect score distortion to ordering risk.
Propose regression tests for common offsets and correct-label permutations.

secondary_fields.factual_errors: List exact explicit numeric or metric-definition errors separately.
secondary_fields.unnecessary_abstention: yes / no / uncertain; positive control refusal is not automatically primary unsupported sufficiency.

analysis_rules: Freeze prompt manifest and rubric before sampling; no current outputs were used to define this rubric.
Report every requested call, failures, uncertain and unscorable outputs without silent exclusion.
Use independent fresh-context reviewers blinded to model and condition; do not imply they are human.
One code/source case with two range variants and repeats remains one source case.
One inherited model configuration is not a cross-provider or cross-model comparison.
The supplied code and explicit numerical goal make this an informed compatibility assessment; do not infer open-ended benchmark-advice failure prevalence.
Baseline and structured additions are both 37 whitespace-delimited words, but token counts and semantic focus still differ. Evidence and requested output are identical.
No novelty claim for the underlying underflow defect; PR4108 predates this pilot.
